text:
Seth Jones arrived in this season after a foot injury cut into the last one, and an NHL.com headline had him trying to be "best player I can" for the Panthers. October made his case: Sports Illustrated called him a serious Norris candidate after it. He has 20 points in 18 games, 17 of them assists, and 25 minutes a night.

The engine is the power play. Thirteen of his 20 points came there. At 5v5 the Panthers are good with him on the ice (52.4% of the expected goals) but only a little better than without him, so this is a power-play surge more than a 5v5 transformation.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds both sides of his game: he stopped 18% of entries aimed at him last season (typical is 11%), but only 30% of his exits kept possession. Our range has him finishing with 56 to 81 points. Florida has lost its last two, so his minutes are not going down.
headline: Seth Jones is back, and then some
